The most informative next analysis is to complete the feature_047 specificity scan on the remaining untested dependency outcomes. If those new comparisons remain small, the conclusion strengthens that feature_047 is an outcome_013-specific dataset association rather than a broad dependency-enhancing marker. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: All twelve new results are valid, have adequate cell counts, and use the registered signed direction: positive estimates mean that feature_047 absence is associated with stronger dependency for the tested outcome. The cross-outcome feature_047 panel mostly strengthens outcome_013 specificity. H52, H53, H56, H57, and H59 are rejected for the original stronger-dependency-when-feature_047-absent claim. H52, H53, H56, and H59 have upper bounds below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold, and H57 has a negative signed estimate with a confidence interval below zero, indicating the opposite direction rather than the claimed association. H57 is notable as a post-hoc opposite-direction candidate: its magnitude is near the 10% threshold for outcome_008, so I registered a reversed comparison as a new hypothesis for later analysis rather than accepting it from a post-hoc scan. H54, H55, H58, H60, H61, and H63 remain unresolved but deferred: their point estimates are small or opposite, and the remaining uncertainty mainly comes from wide intervals that merely include clinically meaningful values. I did not validate these low-priority unresolved candidates. The one active candidate is H62, outcome_013 within feature_060=1. Its signed estimate is +0.0481, about 17.9% of the absolute outcome_013 mean; the discovery confidence interval excludes zero but its lower bound (+0.0100) is still below the 10% threshold. Because this is a subgroup comparison selected from a 12-test panel, multiplicity and confounding/correlation with other features remain plausible competing explanations. Independent validation is therefore useful to test whether the strong outcome_013 association is genuinely preserved in the feature_060=1 stratum. I request validation for H62. No causal or external generalizability claim is being made.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.

Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation

record.narrative: The new validation changes the subgroup interpretation substantially. H37 remains the only feature_047 association supported across discovery and independent validation. For outcome_013, feature_047 absent versus present gives signed discovery estimate +0.0253 and signed validation estimate +0.0301, relative to an absolute mean score of about 0.269; these correspond to approximately 9.4% and 11.2% stronger dependency in the absent group. The validation point exceeds the approximate 10% threshold and the two estimates are direction-concordant, so I accept H37 as a dataset-specific association. However, both intervals include zero and the validation interval is wide after maximum-validation adjustment, so the claim should remain imprecise and noncausal rather than strong or generalizable. H62 is now rejected. Its discovery subgroup estimate within feature_060=1 was unexpectedly large at +0.0481, about 17.9% of the outcome_013 mean, but independent validation reversed to -0.0051 with an interval crossing zero and excluding clinically meaningful positive values in the claimed direction. This is strong evidence that the feature_060=1 subgroup effect is not robust and likely reflected selection/multiplicity after testing multiple strata. H62 failure does not overturn H37, because H37 was supported in the full population by independent validation, but it cautions against inferring stronger marker effects in any particular stratum. The most informative next analysis is validation of H64, the reversed outcome_008 claim suggested by H57: feature_047 present versus absent was associated with signed +0.0282, essentially at the 10% threshold and with a discovery interval excluding zero. Because that direction was discovered post hoc after the original absent-marker claim failed, independent validation is needed before accepting it. record.narrative: No claims are due for assessment. I will run the six currently active, untested comparisons H67-H72. This is the highest-value focused follow-up to accepted H37 and post-hoc H64 candidate: it tests whether predictors with adequate sample overlap show the same conceptual direction as feature_047. Specifically, H67, H69, and H71 test whether an alternative or absent marker state is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency (returned positive estimates support the registered claim), while H68, H70, and H72 test whether an alternative or present marker state is associated with stronger outcome_008 dependency (the opposite-direction pattern suggested by the reversed feature_047 result). I selected feature_063 level_002 versus level_001, feature_045, and feature_008 because they are pre-registered active hypotheses with adequate cell sizes or binary frequency and can test whether the feature_047 pattern is isolated or part of a broader marker pattern. The approximate 10% absolute-mean thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0282 for outcome_008, so results near those values will be treated as clinically meaningful candidate discoveries only if supported by coherent uncertainty. I am not re-running H64-H66 because they already have signed discovery evidence from their parent tests and re-running would not add a new sample. I am also leaving H31 and H32 deferred: they test direct feature_060 main effects within feature_034 strata for outcome_006, but the corresponding interaction H23 failed independent validation and feature_060 effects have generally been weak, so these are lower priority than the predictor-pattern panel. All returned estimates are already signed to the registered direction; positive values support stronger dependency in the hypothesized exposed/alternative/absent group for the registered hypothesis.

Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative: The six new predictor-panel results are valid and adequately powered in every cell. Positive signed estimates support stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative/absent state. For outcome_013, feature_063 level_002 versus level_001 (H67) is small (+0.0029) and its upper bound is below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold (~0.0269), so I reject it. feature_045 absent versus present (H69) is opposite the claimed direction and its upper bound is far below threshold; I reject it. feature_008 absent versus present (H71) has a small point estimate (+0.0101) but an upper bound above threshold, so I leave it unresolved but deferred: the evidence is too weak to prioritize. For outcome_008, feature_063 (H68) is small (+0.0077) but its upper bound just crosses the approximate 10% threshold (~0.0282), so I leave it unresolved/deferred rather than accept it. feature_045 present versus absent (H70) is opposite the claimed direction and below threshold, so I reject it. The one substantive candidate is H72: feature_008 present versus absent is associated with a signed estimate of +0.0322, about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean, and the discovery interval excludes zero. However, the lower bound is far below the clinical threshold and the interval remains wide. Because H72 was selected from a six-test panel and may be confounded by correlated marker features, I do not accept it yet; I request independent validation to determine whether the direction and magnitude are robust. No causal or external generalizability claim is made.

Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: The new validation results close several candidate associations. H72 was the strongest new candidate: feature_008 present versus absent was associated with a signed discovery estimate of +0.0322 for outcome_008, about 11.4% of the absolute outcome_008 mean and above the approximate 10% clinical threshold. However, independent validation reversed the sign to -0.0256, with an adjusted interval from -0.0730 to +0.0218. This provides direct evidence that the discovery result was not robust, likely false-positive selection or confounding among correlated marker features. I therefore reject H72 and close it. H39 has a response deadline. Its discovery estimate (+0.0232) and validation estimate (+0.0187) are directionally positive for feature_023 absent versus present on outcome_009, but both are below the approximate 10% absolute-mean threshold (~0.0256) and their intervals include zero. Thus the claim is not supported at the clinically meaningful magnitude, and I keep it rejected. H42 was validated as a cross-outcome feature_047 check: the validation point estimate is near zero (+0.0001), with an interval of -0.0303 to +0.0305. This is not clinically meaningful and confirms that feature_047 absence does not produce a broad outcome_012 association. Together, these validations strengthen the conclusion that the currently accepted H37 outcome_013 association is relatively outcome-specific rather than part of a broad marker pattern. The most important unresolved candidate is now H64: feature_047 present versus absent for outcome_008. Its discovery evidence is direction-coherent at the clinical threshold (signed +0.0282, about 10%), but it was generated post hoc after the original absent-marker outcome_008 claim failed, so it should not be accepted without independent validation. I registered a small new marker panel for outcome_013 and outcome_008 using feature_042, feature_021, and feature_037 to test whether any other binary markers reproduce either the accepted outcome_013 absent-marker direction or the candidate outcome_008 present-marker direction. If these remain null or opposite, H37 becomes even more isolated; if a new predictor crosses the threshold with coherent uncertainty, it becomes a better validation candidate. No causal or external generalizability claim is made.

Iteration 7/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.

For outcome_013, H73/H75/H77/H79/H81 test whether an absent or 0 state of feature_042, feature_021, feature_037, feature_002, or feature_034 is associated with stronger dependency; for outcome_008, H74/H76/H78/H80/H82 test whether a present or 1 state of the same predictors is associated with stronger dependency. These are not causal tests; they test whether the apparent feature_047 pattern is isolated or reproduced by other measured markers. The approximate absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0269 for outcome_013 and 0.0282 for outcome_008. Because this is a multi-test panel, I will not accept a near-threshold result without a coherent interval and, where useful, independent validation. I also selected H31 and H32 to use the remaining analysis slots productively: they test direct feature_060 main effects within feature_034=1 and feature_034=0 for outcome_006. These were deferred after the feature_060-by-feature_034 interaction H23 failed validation, but the main-effect cells have not been directly tested. The outcome_006 mean is small (about -0.093), so the 10% absolute-mean threshold is only about 0.0093; results should therefore be judged cautiously and preferably with independent validation if strong. I am not rerunning H64-H66 because their comparisons are mathematically equivalent to already tested reversed parents and would not add a new sample. All returned estimates and intervals are already signed to each registered hypothesis direction, so positive values support stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative state and negative values do not.

Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

Positive signed estimates support the registered direction (stronger dependency in the registered exposed/alternative/absent state), whereas negative signed estimates oppose it. For outcome_013, the clinical threshold is about 0.0269; for outcome_008 it is about 0.0282; for outcome_006 it is about 0.0093. Most marker-panel main effects are null or too weak to prioritize. H73 (R73), H77 (R77), and H79 (R79) are rejected/closed because their entire signed intervals for the claimed direction lie below the relevant clinical threshold. H76 (R76) and H78 (R78) are rejected/closed for the registered present-stronger claim because the positive-signed portions of their intervals are below threshold; their raw opposite signals are not sufficiently supported to override the original hypotheses. H75 (R75), H80 (R80), H81 (R81), and H82 (R82) remain unresolved/deferred because point estimates are below threshold, intervals include zero, and only upper bounds cross the clinical threshold; there is too much uncertainty to accept or validate them now. That signed negative result corresponds to a robust raw opposite effect: feature_042 present is associated with a less negative outcome_008 score, with raw magnitude about 0.0295, slightly above threshold. Because this emerged from a multiplicity-prone marker panel, I do not accept the opposite effect now, but I registered a parent-linked reversal proposal so it can be assessed and validated separately. record.narrative: The delivered validation evidence closes two post hoc feature_047 candidates. H62 tested whether feature_047 absent versus present was associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency within the feature_060=1 subgroup. record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The only accepted claim remains H37: in this dataset, feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency. The leading unresolved dataset-specific candidate is H83, the parent-linked reversal for outcome_008 and feature_042. Its signed discovery estimate is about +0.0295, just above the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical threshold for outcome_008 (~0.0282), with a 95% discovery interval excluding zero; however, it arose from multiplicity-prone marker screening and has not been independently validated. I therefore register refinements that test whether H83 is robust or driven by measured confounders/effect modifiers. Specifically, I propose feature_042 absent-versus-present tests within the complementary feature_047=0 stratum, within balanced feature_034=1 and feature_034=0 strata, and formal interactions by feature_034 and feature_047. These do not prove causality, but they ask whether the raw direction (feature_042 absent associated with more negative outcome_008) is stable across major strata or appears only in one subgroup. If H83 remains coherent across H84, the feature_047=0 test, and/or feature_034 tests, it will be the strongest candidate for independent validation in a later appraise stage; if it is null or opposite in strata, I will downweight it without validation.

I also register subgroup localizations of the accepted H37 association after H62 failed validation. Feature_060=0 is the complement of the failed feature_060=1 subgroup, and feature_034=0 complements the imprecise positive feature_034=1 subgroup test H61. The registered hypothesis is that feature_047 absent remains associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency in these strata, with expected negative raw exposed-minus-comparator values and hence positive signed estimates. If these follow-ups are broadly consistent, H37 is less likely to be a narrow subgroup artifact; if they are discordant, the accepted main effect remains dataset-specific but heterogeneous. For the active H31 outcome_006 subgroup candidate, I register a smaller test within feature_034=1 and feature_047=1 to see whether the large feature_060-present stronger signal survives in the larger feature_047=1 subgroup. Because H31's corresponding interaction H23 failed validation, this is lower-priority than the H83 robustness program and should not be validated unless the subgroup result remains stable and compelling.

Finally, I add two exploratory feature_055 comparisons because feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 has known adequate cell sizes and provides an independent probe of whether a common categorical marker is associated with either the accepted outcome_013 signal or the candidate outcome_008 signal. These are initially uncertain (anticipated_direction 0), and I will require clinically meaningful point estimates with coherent uncertainty before treating them as meaningful.

record.narrative: I assessed all new discovery results with signed estimates interpreted directly in the registered direction. Approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0093 for outcome_006. record.narrative: The new validations are decisive and negative for the leading feature_042/outcome_008 candidate. H83 tested feature_042 absent versus present as stronger outcome_008 dependency; its signed discovery estimate was +0.0295, but independent validation was -0.0105 with adjusted interval -0.0458 to +0.0248. That validation is in the opposite direction, includes zero, and is below the approximate outcome_008 clinical threshold near 0.0282. I therefore reject and close H83. The opposite original claim H74 is also not supported: validation gave only +0.0105 with interval -0.0248 to +0.0458, while discovery was significantly opposite. Because the main feature_042/outcome_008 effect failed validation, I close the active stratum refinements H84 and H86 as dataset-specific post hoc leads rather than accepting them. For the response deadlines, H72 validation reversed/nullified the feature_008 present-stronger outcome_008 claim (-0.0256, adjusted CI -0.0730 to +0.0218), and H42 validation showed essentially no feature_047 absent versus present effect on outcome_012 (+0.0001, adjusted CI -0.0303 to +0.0305); both remain rejected and closed. H19, the feature_055 level_003 versus level_001 probe for outcome_010, validated as null (+0.0049, adjusted CI -0.0289 to +0.0387) and is rejected and closed. The supported finding remains only H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency in this dataset, though its intervals remain uncertain and the association should not be interpreted as causal or externally generalizable. The next most informative candidate is H95, the reversed feature_055 probe for outcome_008: level_001 versus level_003 has signed discovery +0.0315 with 95% discovery interval +0.0018 to +0.0611, just above the clinical threshold, but it was generated after an opposite original H94 probe and has no independent validation. I keep H95 active and plan validation as the priority if it remains useful. I registered feature_034 and feature_047 stratum/effect-modification diagnostics for H95, but the outcome_006 subgroup leads H31/H92 remain secondary because H23 failed validation.

Iteration 9/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

record.narrative:
No assessments are due. The only accepted dataset-specific finding remains H37: feature_047 absent versus present is associated with stronger outcome_013 dependency, but its subgroup localization is heterogeneous. I therefore register a formal interaction by feature_034 to ask whether the accepted H37 effect is genuinely modified by feature_034 rather than only appearing different in separately estimated subgroups. A clinically meaningful interaction would change the interpretation from a broad but heterogeneous main effect to a stratified association; a near-null or imprecise interaction would support treating subgroup contrasts as descriptive only.

The main unresolved candidate is H95, outcome_008 with feature_055 level_001 versus level_003. Its signed discovery estimate is threshold-near, but it is post hoc because it was registered after the opposite feature_055 probe failed. Before spending another validation slot, I propose level-level refinements. Comparing level_001 with level_002 asks whether level_002 behaves more like the putative stronger-dependency level_001 group or like level_003. Comparing level_002 with level_003 asks whether level_002 sits intermediate between the level_001 and level_003 contrast or is unrelated. Because feature_055 levels are nominal, I do not assume a numeric gradient; the hypotheses are specific group contrasts with plausible null or opposite outcomes. If level_001 versus level_002 and level_002 versus level_003 are coherent with the main contrast, this would strengthen H95 as a validation candidate. If they are discordant, H95 should be downweighted even if the main contrast remains nominally positive.

I also register a formal feature_034 interaction for H95 because H97 separately estimates the feature_034=1 stratum, while the complement is only implicit. This tests whether any level_001-versus-level_003 effect is concentrated in feature_034=1. The corresponding feature_047 interaction was already registered as H99; together these can determine whether H95 is stable or driven by one major stratum.

Finally, I keep the outcome_006 subgroup program as secondary. H92 showed a strong feature_060 present versus absent effect in the nested feature_034=1 and feature_047=1 cell, while H96 remains pending for the feature_047=0 complement. I register a direct interaction by feature_047 within feature_034=1 to test whether the feature_060 association is genuinely concentrated in feature_047=1. This is important because the earlier broader outcome_006 interaction H23 failed validation; a direct positive interaction would be more compelling than nested cell estimates alone, but it still must be treated cautiously because it is subgroup-specific and post hoc.

I am not requesting validation in this explore stage. The next analysis should populate these diagnostics. If H95 diagnostics remain coherent and threshold-near or stronger, H95 should be the next validation target. If they are inconsistent, I will close the feature_055/outcome_008 candidate without validation and redirect to the outcome_006 nested program or accepted-H37 localization only.

record.narrative:
I assessed the new discovery evidence using signed estimates interpreted directly in the registered direction. For reference, approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical thresholds are about 0.0282 for outcome_008, 0.0269 for outcome_013, and 0.0093 for outcome_006. H100 tests level_001 versus level_002 for outcome_008 and gives a near-null signed estimate (-0.0006; 95% discovery interval -0.0320 to +0.0307). I reject and close this specific level_001-versus-level_002 claim. However, H101 tests level_002 versus level_003 and gives +0.0321 (95% interval +0.0014 to +0.0628), a threshold-near positive effect. Together with the main H95 estimate of +0.0315 and H100's null between level_001 and level_002, the data suggest a plausible nominal-group pattern in which level_001 and level_002 behave similarly and are more strongly associated with outcome_008 dependency than level_003. This coherence makes H95 worth independent validation, but it does not justify accepting H95 or H101 yet: the main interval lower bound is below clinical relevance, H95 is a reversed post hoc probe after H94, and multiple feature_055 level contrasts were examined. H101 is therefore kept active but unresolved as a competing or supporting nominal contrast.

The feature_034 diagnostics do not argue against H95. H97, within feature_034=1, gives +0.0278 (interval -0.0118 to +0.0675), near but just below the outcome_008 threshold. H102, the formal feature_034 interaction, is near null (-0.0081; interval -0.0675 to +0.0514). I reject and close H102 as unsupported effect modification, and defer H97 because the stratum estimate is imprecise. These results indicate that the feature_055 outcome_008 signal is not obviously created by feature_034 effect modification. The feature_047 diagnostics are more cautionary but not decisive. H98, within the large feature_047=1 stratum, gives +0.0268 (interval -0.0066 to +0.0601), just below threshold and imprecise. H99, the formal feature_047 interaction, is negative in the registered signed scale and very imprecise (-0.0230; interval -0.0960 to +0.0500). I close H99 unresolved because it does not support a clinically meaningful feature_047 interaction and I do not want to spend validation on it, but I do not treat it as proof that feature_047 is irrelevant. Overall, H95 remains the leading dataset-specific candidate because its main estimate is threshold-near and the level coherence is plausible, but it needs independent validation before acceptance.

For outcome_006, H96 estimates feature_060 present versus absent in the feature_047=0 complement of the earlier positive feature_047=1 nested cell. The signed estimate is -0.0152 (interval -0.1223 to +0.0920), opposite to the claimed direction and very imprecise in only 95 versus 95 observations. I reject and close H96. H103, the direct feature_047 interaction within feature_034=1, gives +0.0763 (interval -0.0417 to +0.1942). Although the point estimate is large, the interval is far too wide and the complement estimate from H96 is discordant; combined with the prior validation failure of H23, this closes the outcome_006 subgroup program as insufficiently supported. For the accepted H37 feature_047/outcome_013 association, H104 provides the formal feature_034 interaction: -0.0053 (interval -0.0592 to +0.0486), near null. I reject and close it as unsupported modification, supporting interpretation of H37 as a broad dataset-specific association rather than a claim of feature_034 stratification. I request validation for H95 because it is the most informative eligible unresolved candidate; independent validation will test reproducibility in the supplied dataset framework without implying causality or external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.
