record.narrative: I audited the new discovery evidence using the signed-direction convention: for all direction -1 outcome_006 and outcome_014 tests, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group or exposed level is associated with a more negative CRISPR dependency score. The approximate 10% absolute-mean benchmark for outcome_006 and outcome_014 is about 0.0093, because their overall means are near -0.093. I accepted only comparisons whose full signed 95% interval exceeded this benchmark and whose cells met the size requirement. H254 is the only new result meeting that standard: within outcome_014, feature_006 present versus absent has signed estimate +0.0647 with 95% interval +0.0108 to +0.1186 and adequate cells (161 vs 1839). I therefore accept H254 as a dataset-specific measured association: feature_006 present is associated with a more negative outcome_014 dependency score. This result should be treated cautiously because it is rare-exposed, unvalidated, and emerged after many comparisons. The other new outcome_006 residual-marker tests are inconclusive for the registered direction: H237, H246, H249, H251, H252, and H256 have positive point estimates in some cases above the point benchmark, but their lower bounds cross null or fall below the clinical benchmark, so they cannot be accepted as clinically meaningful and are closed as unresolved. H247, H250, H253, and H255 have negative point estimates opposite the registered direction and do not support the stated hypothesis; they are rejected. H248 is important to interpret carefully: the registered direction was negative raw dependency in feature_007 present versus absent within feature_021=0, but the reported signed interval is entirely negative, implying a raw opposite association with feature_007 present associated with less negative outcome_006. The raw opposite magnitude is large (point about +0.038), but the lower absolute bound is only about 0.0081, below the approximate 0.0093 clinical benchmark. Thus I reject the registered direction and do not promote a reversed clinically meaningful claim; it remains at most a borderline, multiplicity-sensitive signal. I also closed H245 because it has been tested and does not meet the clinical benchmark criterion: the signed lower bound is positive but far below the 10% threshold. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so no validation was requested. These conclusions are associations measured in this supplied dataset only and are not causal, mechanistic, leakage-free, or externally generalizable claims.

Iteration 20/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: No new validation was released and there are no assessments due or validation response deadlines. Independent validation capacity is exhausted, so this synthesis records final dataset-specific conclusions from existing evidence and closes remaining untested low-priority nominal screens rather than expanding supplied-data subgroup mining. The strongest supported finding is H107: outcome_006, feature_021 absent versus present, direction -1, signed +0.8019 (95% CI +0.7823 to +0.8216), independently validated at +0.8115 (95% CI +0.7821 to +0.8408). Because estimates are signed, the raw exposed-minus-comparator difference is negative: feature_021 absent is associated with much more negative outcome_006 dependency scores than feature_021 present. This exceeds the operational 10 percent benchmark by a very large margin and is stable across many tested marker strata; no interaction robustly modifies it. Secondary supported association: H111 outcome_006 feature_020 absent versus present, signed +0.0595 (95% CI +0.0148 to +0.1043), discovery-only, above benchmark but unvalidated. Accepted refinements: H195 within feature_060=0, signed +0.0881 (95% CI +0.0214 to +0.1548); H197 within feature_002=1, signed +0.0853 (95% CI +0.0215 to +0.1492); H233 within feature_021=1 and feature_060=0, signed +0.0681 (95% CI +0.0099 to +0.1262), borderline and small comparator. New dataset-specific accepted association: H254 outcome_014 feature_006 present versus absent, signed +0.0647 (95% CI +0.0108 to +0.1186), meaning feature_006 present is associated with more negative outcome_014 dependency; it meets the benchmark but is rare exposed, unvalidated, and multiplicity-sensitive. Negative findings dominate: many initial positive associations failed independent validation or remained below clinical relevance, including outcome_008 feature_047 (H57/H64), outcome_013 feature_047 within feature_060=1 (H62), outcome_008 feature_008 (H72), outcome_008 feature_042 (H74/H83), outcome_008 feature_055 contrasts (H94/H95), outcome_005 feature_021 (H154), and outcome_010 feature_055 (H19). Interaction tests generally did not establish effect modification. The latest outcome_006/outcome_014 screens mostly produced null, opposite, or below-benchmark results; the only new accepted association is H254. Unresolved uncertainty remains for feature_020 localization and specificity, especially H171, H178, H225, H230, H189, H192, H194, H198, and marker intersections; H37 outcome_013 feature_047 is borderline unresolved with validation interval +0.0301 (95% CI -0.0095 to +0.0696). The borderline opposite feature_007 outcome_006 signal in H248 is not clinically meaningful and was not reversed. Overall, the robust finding is outcome_006 feature_021 absent versus present; the most useful next analysis is strict pre-specified external validation of feature_020 absent outcome_006 associations and, more cautiously, H254 outcome_014 feature_006, not further post-hoc mining in the supplied dataset. All claims remain observational associations with opaque predictor labels, not causal or biologically mechanistic conclusions.

Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.

only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed the twelve new discovery results using the signed-direction convention: for direction -1 claims, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group or exposed level is associated with a more negative CRISPR dependency score. For outcome_006 and outcome_014, whose overall means are approximately -0.093, the approximate 10% absolute-mean clinical benchmark is about 0.0093. H259 and H260 replicate the dominant outcome_006 feature_021 absent-versus-present association within feature_052 strata: H259 gives signed +0.79735 (95% CI +0.77666 to +0.81805) and H260 gives +0.82539 (95% CI +0.76594 to +0.88484). Both full intervals are far above the clinical benchmark and have valid cell sizes, so I accept them as dataset-specific measured associations and close investigation because no independent validation capacity remains. The remaining new results do not justify acceptance. H261, H263, H240, H116, H122, and H242 are registered-positive hypotheses with negative signed point estimates and intervals crossing zero or lying largely on the opposite side; they do not support the registered direction and are rejected as supported dataset associations. H262 and H241 have clinically sized positive point estimates, but their lower bounds cross zero and are below the benchmark, so they are scientifically unresolved and only worth external validation, not supplied-data acceptance. H239 and H115 have very small positive point estimates with wide intervals that can include clinically meaningful values, but the observed effects and the multiplicity burden make further supplied-data follow-up low priority; I close them as unresolved. From a critical-review standpoint, accepted effects remain observational, use opaque predictor labels, may reflect leakage or dataset-specific structure, and have been screened through many comparisons. H263 is particularly informative for the earlier rare outcome_014 feature_006 finding: it provides no evidence that the same predictor affects outcome_006, so H254 should remain cautious and outcome-specific. No validation was requested because remaining_new_requests=0. All conclusions are limited to this supplied dataset and do not imply causality, mechanism, or external generalizability.

Iteration 21/25, stage synthesize, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess new validation and any response deadlines listed below. Explain what you conclude and what to investigate next. Accepted claims update automatically.

record.narrative: No new validation was released at this synthesis, and no assessments are due; independent validation capacity is exhausted. The principal conclusion from the supplied dataset is a large, replicated, dataset-specific association between outcome_006 and feature_021. With the registered direction -1, positive signed estimates mean that the exposed condition, feature_021 absent, has a more negative CRISPR dependency score than feature_021 present. The overall contrast H107 is signed +0.8019, 95% CI +0.7823 to +0.8216 (R118), with independent validation +0.8115, CI +0.7821 to +0.8408 under the stricter validation alpha (R121). The raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast is approximately -0.80, far exceeding the operational 10 percent clinical benchmark for outcome_006 and remaining stable in tested strata, including feature_052=0 and feature_052=1 in H259 and H260. Interaction tests generally did not establish effect modification. A secondary supported but unvalidated association is H111, outcome_006 feature_020 absent versus present, signed +0.0595, CI +0.0148 to +0.1043 (R157). Some accepted strata, such as H195, H197, and H233, localize parts of this signal, but the exact independence from feature_021 and other markers remains uncertain. A cautious accepted discovery is H254, outcome_014 feature_006 present versus absent, signed +0.0647, CI +0.0108 to +0.1186 (R237); the exposed group is rare, the evidence is discovery-only and multiplicity-sensitive, and specificity testing H263 did not support the same predictor for outcome_006. Negative findings dominate the rest of the search. Validated or repeated null, below-benchmark, or opposite candidate associations include H19 for outcome_010 feature_055, H23 for an outcome_006 feature_060 interaction, H39 for outcome_009 feature_023, H42 and H57/H64 for outcome_008/outcome_012 feature_047, H62 for outcome_013 feature_047 within feature_060=1, H72 for outcome_008 feature_008, H74/H83 for outcome_008 feature_042, H94/H95 for outcome_008 feature_055 contrasts, and H154 for outcome_005 feature_021. Many other screens across the 16 outcomes were either clinically trivial, imprecise, opposite, or unsupported. For direction -1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group or level has a more negative dependency score than the comparator; for direction +1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed group or level is less negative than the comparator. I will require the full signed 95% lower bound to exceed an approximate 10% absolute-mean benchmark before accepting: about 0.0093 for outcome_006 and outcome_014, and about 0.0269 for outcome_013; rare-level tests remain exploratory because of imprecision. Priority 1: test additional categorical predictors on the primary outcome_006 with known large marginal cells or known adequate level counts: feature_048 level_001 versus level_003 and rare level_002 versus level_003; feature_036 level_001 versus level_002, using direction +1 because weak prior evidence from a different outcome suggested level_001 may be less negative; and feature_055 level_001 versus level_002. Priority 2: refine candidate binary predictors. Feature_007 showed a significant opposite-direction stratum-specific pattern in H248 (present less negative within feature_021=0), so I test the full population with direction +1. Feature_011 showed a positive but imprecise present-versus-absent signal within feature_021=0 in H249, so I test the full population with direction -1. Feature_052 remains unresolved in H262; I localize it further to feature_020=0 and feature_021=0. Feature_028 level_003 versus level_002 has a clinically sized but imprecise overall estimate in H241; I test it in the common feature_047=1 stratum. Priority 3: assess specificity of the cautious outcome_014 feature_006 finding by testing feature_006 on outcome_013. These are dataset-specific measured associations only; conditional cells are expected to be adequate but are not guaranteed by marginal counts, so the controller must enforce the minimum cell-size rule. No causal, mechanistic, leakage-free, or generalizable claims are made.

Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous

refinements to the earlier parent claim.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using

For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

Given the large number of screened comparisons and the possibility of confounding by the dominant feature_021 association, I cannot accept it as scientifically meaningful on this evidence alone. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.

subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.

and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;

and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

refinements to the earlier parent claim.

censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.

is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator

number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

record.narrative: Assessment follows the signed-direction convention: for a direction -1 claim, a positive signed estimate means the exposed condition is associated with a more negative dependency score, whereas for a direction +1 claim, a positive signed estimate means the exposed condition is less negative than the comparator. I used the conservative supplied-data benchmark of approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean, about 0.0093 for outcome_006 and outcome_014, and required the full signed lower bound to exceed that benchmark before accepting a discovery-only or subgroup association. The strongest new accepted result is H275: within feature_007 present, feature_021 absent versus present gives signed +0.7635, 95% CI +0.7137 to +0.8132, cell sizes 157/49. This is a very large, clinically meaningful and statistically robust dataset-specific association, and it shows that the dominant feature_021 signal is not eliminated in the rare feature_007 present subgroup. H276 is also accepted: in the feature_021 absent majority, feature_006 present versus absent on outcome_014 gives signed +0.0773, CI +0.0163 to +0.1384, with lower bound well above the outcome_014 benchmark; this strengthens the already accepted outcome-specific H254 association. H280 is accepted more cautiously because it is the secondary feature_020 candidate localized in the feature_007 absent majority: signed +0.0579, CI +0.0101 to +0.1058, cell sizes 1497/297. Its lower bound just exceeds the benchmark, so it supports H111 but remains a discovery-only, multiplicity-sensitive association. By contrast, H273 tests feature_007 within feature_021 present and gives a small opposite signed estimate, -0.0050, CI -0.0505 to +0.0405; together with the overall H268 lower bound below the clinical benchmark and the H274 interaction null/opposite result, I reject H268 and its robustness tests as not established as scientifically meaningful. H274 is not accepted as a positive feature_007 interaction with feature_021 present: the signed estimate is negative, -0.0428, and the interval includes zero, with no clinically meaningful positive lower bound. H277 remains unresolved and deferred: feature_006 on outcome_014 within feature_021 present gives a clinically sized positive signed estimate, +0.0272, but the interval is very wide and includes zero, so the rare subgroup does not establish the effect. H278 is unresolved and deferred as a possible modification of the feature_006 association by feature_021, but the claimed direction is not supported: the interaction estimate is -0.0501 with a wide interval including zero. H279 remains unresolved and deferred because the feature_020 contrast within feature_007 present is clinically sized, +0.0540, but the rare comparator gives a very wide interval crossing zero. Among the four additional screened binary comparisons, H113, H125, and H147 are rejected as unsupported or clinically trivial: H113 and H125 are small and opposite to their registered positive-direction claims, and H147 is far below the benchmark despite wide uncertainty. H148 remains unresolved and deferred because feature_046 has a clinically sized positive signed estimate, +0.0399, but the interval includes zero and extends below the benchmark, leaving only low-confidence signal. No independent validation can be requested because voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. All accepted statements remain observational associations in this supplied dataset with opaque predictor labels; they do not establish causality, mechanism, leakage-free biological interpretation, or external generalizability.

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep

with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.

record.narrative:
FINAL SCIENTIFIC REPORT.

No new independent validation was released in this synthesis, and voluntary validation capacity is exhausted. The conclusions below are dataset-specific observational associations with opaque predictor labels; they do not establish causality, mechanism, leakage-free biology, or external generalizability.

SUPPORTED FINDINGS.
H107 is the principal supported finding. For outcome_006, feature_021 absent versus present under direction -1 gives a signed discovery estimate of +0.8019 with 95% CI +0.7823 to +0.8216, R118, and independent validation +0.8115 with validation CI +0.7821 to +0.8408 under the stricter multiplicity-adjusted alpha, R121. Because returned estimates are already signed and more negative dependency scores mean stronger dependency, this indicates that feature_021 absence is associated with a much stronger outcome_006 dependency than feature_021 presence. The effect is far above the conservative clinical benchmark of roughly 0.0093 for outcome_006 and is replicated independently.
H275 shows that the same feature_021 absent-versus-present signal persists in the rare feature_007-present subgroup: signed +0.7635, CI +0.7137 to +0.8132, R266.
H111 and H280 are secondary supported but unvalidated associations for outcome_006: feature_020 absent versus present gives signed +0.0595, CI +0.0148 to +0.1043, R157, and within feature_007 absent gives signed +0.0579, CI +0.0101 to +0.1058, R271. These are clinically sized relative to outcome_006, but they remain discovery-only, multiplicity-sensitive, and dependent on the possibility that the feature_020 and feature_021 predictors encode overlapping structure.
H254 and H276 support an outcome_014 association for feature_006 presence: full-population signed +0.0647, CI +0.0108 to +0.1186, R237, and within feature_021 absent signed +0.0773, CI +0.0163 to +0.1384, R267. Under direction -1, positive signed estimates mean feature_006-present scores are more negative, i.e., stronger dependency. This is also discovery-only and has not been independently validated.

NEGATIVE AND REJECTED RESULTS.
I reassessed H282 and reject it. Within feature_021 absent, feature_007 present versus absent under direction +1 gives signed +0.0378, CI +0.0081 to +0.0675, R231. The interval is above zero, but its lower bound is below the clinical benchmark, so the evidence does not establish a scientifically meaningful feature_007 association in this subgroup. This is consistent with rejecting H268, H273, and H274, and feature_007 should not be presented as a robust clinically meaningful predictor. H281 and H283 are closed as unresolved because no usable evidence became available.
Rejected or unsupported results dominate the broader search. These include validated or repeated below-benchmark, null, or opposite findings such as H19, H23, H37, H39, H42, H57/H64, H62, H72, H74/H83, H94/H95, and H154, as well as numerous screened binary or categorical contrasts that are small, imprecise, opposite to the registered direction, or below the clinical benchmark. Negative results here mean that the supplied dataset does not support scientifically meaningful differences at the chosen threshold; they do not prove absence of effects in the broader world.

UNRESOLVED UNCERTAINTY.
Several candidates remain unresolved and should not be treated as established findings. H277 and H278 leave outcome_014 feature_006 within the rare feature_021-present setting uncertain and imprecise. H279 leaves feature_020 within feature_007-present uncertain because the interval is wide. H148 and H128 leave feature_046 and feature_023 as low-confidence outcome_006 candidates. Rare predictor contrasts, including some feature_028 level contrasts and other rare subgroup estimates, remain unresolved because cells are small and intervals are wide. Multiplicity from broad screening further lowers confidence in any single unresolved candidate.

MOST INFORMATIVE NEXT ANALYSIS.
The highest-value next step is strict pre-specified external or fully held-out validation with no further post-hoc mining. Primary endpoint: outcome_006, feature_021 absent versus present. Secondary endpoints: outcome_006 feature_020 absent versus present and outcome_014 feature_006 present versus absent. Pre-specify a small set of effect-modification checks by feature_021 and feature_007 for the secondary candidates, using multiplicity-adjusted intervals and requiring clinically meaningful lower bounds. If internal analysis continues, restrict it to targeted robustness of H107 and the few secondary associations rather than broad new screening. All final claims remain limited to observational associations in the supplied dataset.

Iteration 24/25, stage explore, attempt 1.
Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Propose scientifically useful new comparisons or refinements for later analysis.

The direction convention remains unchanged: for direction -1 claims with exposed=0/comparator=1, a positive signed estimate means the exposed condition has a more negative CRISPR dependency score than the comparator; for exposed=1/comparator=0, a positive signed estimate also means the exposed condition is more negative. The first two proposals refine the principal accepted H107 feature_021 absent-versus-present association on outcome_006 by localizing it in the majority feature_007-absent setting and further stratifying by feature_047 or feature_020. This asks whether the large replicated signal remains when potentially correlated binary predictors are held fixed. The next two proposals refine the accepted outcome_014 feature_006 association H254/H276 by restricting to feature_021-absent plus either feature_047-positive or feature_007-absent, testing robustness to other predictors and not just the broad feature_021 stratum. The following three proposals refine the secondary feature_020 outcome_006 signal H111/H280 within feature_007-absent, then split by feature_021 absent/present and add feature_047 stratification; this distinguishes whether feature_020 is independent, confounded, or effect-modified by the dominant feature_021 signal. The outcome_008 feature_006 comparison is a deliberately open specificity test: if feature_006 is only associated with outcome_014, this outcome should be null or below the outcome_008 clinical benchmark; if it shows a clinically meaningful effect, that would broaden the interpretation. Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.

comparison cell.

hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released

deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.

the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.

For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Assess the newly delivered discovery evidence. Optionally set validate to one eligible claim reference for independent validation; omit it for no request. The controller attaches the discovery result. Validation arrives after this stage.

record.narrative: I assessed the newly delivered comparisons using the already signed estimates and the conservative supplied-data benchmark of approximately 10% of the absolute outcome mean: about 0.0093 for outcome_006 and outcome_014, and about 0.028 for outcome_008. A discovery claim was accepted only if the full signed lower bound exceeded that benchmark, not merely the point estimate. H281, H284, and H285 are accepted robustness confirmations of the principal feature_021 absent-versus-present association on outcome_006. Within feature_007 absent, H281 gives +0.8063 (CI +0.7849 to +0.8276); within feature_007 absent and feature_047=1, H284 gives +0.8059 (CI +0.7820 to +0.8297); and within feature_007 absent and feature_020=0, H285 gives +0.8009 (CI +0.7770 to +0.8248). These are enormous, clinically meaningful, and precise associations, showing that the dominant feature_021 signal is not attenuated by holding feature_007 absent, feature_047 positive, or feature_020 absent. They are therefore strong dataset-specific robustness checks, though not new independent validation. H286 and H287 test whether the accepted outcome_014 feature_006 association persists in narrower feature_021-absent settings. H286 is imprecise, with +0.0562 and CI -0.0124 to +0.1248, so the restricted subgroup is not established. H287 is positive and its interval excludes zero (+0.0686, CI +0.0027 to +0.1346), but its lower bound is below the clinical benchmark, so it does not support a scientifically meaningful effect in that restricted feature_007-absent subgroup. Research goal: investigate which measured predictors and subgroups are associated with scientifically meaningful differences in outcome_012 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_005 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_015 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_002 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_016 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_007 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_013 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_014 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_004 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_009 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_010 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_001 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_008 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_003 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_006 (CRISPR dependency score), outcome_011 (CRISPR dependency score). Use the supplied dataset to discover and follow up comparisons, assess effect sizes and uncertainty, and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Use independent validation when useful and distinguish findings in this dataset from claims about causality or generalizability.
Each iteration proceeds through explore (propose comparisons), analyze (request tests), appraise (assess the resulting discovery evidence and optionally request validation), and synthesize (assess validation and update conclusions and plans).

Study instructions:
Investigate diverse, scientifically meaningful comparisons and use previous
results to allocate further investigation. Broad exploration and focused follow-up are both useful
throughout the run. Assess discoveries in this supplied dataset and use independent validation when
useful. Biological interpretation and generalizability may remain uncertain.

Register comparisons, anticipated directions, and initial assessments before requesting analyses.
The controller assigns claim references. For a changed claim, propose a new comparison and link
refinements to the earlier parent claim.
Clinical log_pfs_months is natural log progression-free survival in months, fully observed without
censoring. Dependency scores are continuous; more negative values mean stronger dependency.
A mean_difference is exposed minus comparator within eligibility and subgroup. An interaction
subtracts that comparison in the subgroup complement in the same eligible population.
Use your scientific judgment to assess the size, uncertainty, and importance of each effect
and decide which conclusions the evidence supports. Explain your reasoning in the narrative.
Returned estimates and intervals are ALREADY SIGNED to the indicated hypothesis direction. Do not
multiply them by direction again. For example, raw -0.4 with direction -1 is reported as +0.4.
Discovery analyses use 95% Welch intervals and need at least 20 observations in every
comparison cell.

Each iteration has explore, analyze, appraise, and synthesize stages. Every stage may register
hypotheses for later analysis. Analyze selects up to 12 previously registered hypotheses.
Appraise assesses every new discovery result, records active/deferred/closed investigation, and may
request validation after considering those results. At most one new voluntary validation request
is allowed per iteration and ten per run. Cached requests reuse the same evidence. The evaluator
may also deliver scheduled validation during the run. Independent intervals account for the maximum
number of validation comparisons in the run. Results arrive before synthesis. Assess newly released
validation immediately in synthesis and explicitly reassess the original claim when its response
deadline appears in the context, even if you also investigate a refinement. The controller maintains
the accepted claim set from your assessments; you do not need to repeat that list. Explanations are
retained for inspection. Acceptance does not require prior independent validation.

Predictor names and text categorical values use opaque labels. Levels are nominal labels, not ordered numbers. Numeric values, outcome scales, and missingness are preserved.


You are investigating the supplied research dataset. Return one JSON object using
only this stage's response form. The service performs analyses; you choose the science.
For this task, a relative difference in outcome of 10% or greater is considered clinically significant.
Use your judgment about uncertainty and conclusions in light of this clinical significance threshold. Acceptance does not require
independent validation first. Explain your reasoning in narrative.

The ledger contains every registered claim, its current assessment, and all its available direct
evidence. References H1, H2, ... identify claims; R1, R2, ... identify evidence. Copy these short
references when needed. New proposals receive references automatically after this stage. A changed
comparison or reversed claim is a new proposal, optionally linked to an existing parent.
Proposal direction is the claim (+1 positive, -1 negative); anticipated_direction is your
expectation
of the raw exposed-minus-comparator contrast before seeing evidence (-1, 0 uncertain, +1).
initial_status is your assessment at registration. These initial judgments are recorded once.
If a proposal repeats an existing claim, the controller preserves that claim's current assessment;
use assessments to change a scientific conclusion.

For each claim in assessments_due, return one assessment with claim,
status (accept/reject/unresolved),
and investigation (active/deferred/closed). You may also reassess other claims. Omitted claims keep
their current assessment. Assess the original claim even when proposing a refinement or reversal.
By omitting evidence in an assessment, you assess all evidence displayed on that claim's card;
the controller attaches those references. To specify a subset or related evidence, provide evidence
with short R references; include the evidence listed in assessments_due for that claim.
An unchanged assessment or an investigation-only change can use evidence: [];
changing accept/reject/unresolved requires available evidence. Bookkeeping does not satisfy a due
evidence assessment.
For a refinement, parent identifies the earlier claim; omitted motivating_evidence attaches the
parent's displayed evidence. These automatic links record evidence supplied for your assessment
or refinement, not proof that you discussed or understood every result.

The controller maintains the accepted set from your assessments. Do not reconstruct it. Optional
research_notes replaces your persistent notebook; omit it to keep the existing notes. Use it for
plans or reasoning worth retaining. Latest stage narratives are also retained. All earlier numerical
evidence remains in the ledger. Do not repeat completed actions or old responses.
Omit unused fields.

Your action now: Select up to 12 existing claim references in run_analyses. This requests analyses now; previously tested comparisons reuse their data and give no new sample. New results enter the ledger after this form is accepted and are assessed in appraise. Any assessment in this form must use evidence already in the supplied ledger.
